purpose: First live 10-turn semantic-continuity canary for the Claude Code Max Subscription runtime family (Runtime/Provider matrix row claude_code, previously NOT RUN). Reuses the exact 9-fact contract from docs/evidence/keeper-multiturn-codex-live-2026-08-13T155130Z.json for direct cross-runtime comparability.

runtime.selection_reason: Base/default tier of the family (sonnet), matching the 'sonnet 계열' precedent set for representative selection.

facts_established_in_turns_1_to_9: The project codename is Aster Ledger.
The prototype city is Nacre Bay.
Cobalt tokens must be processed before amber tokens.
If sensor Delta-7 goes silent, pause the shipment but retain the queue.
Dr. Iona Vale owns the recovery decision.
Recovery is confirmed by three consecutive violet pulses.
After confirmation, the retained queue moves to Orchid Pier.
The final recovery notice goes to channel Harbor-3.
Amber tokens tagged glasswing are quarantined rather than shipped, while cobalt remains first.

stray_autonomous_turn_before_contract_st.note: Keepalive heartbeat at boot, before proactive_enabled=false had propagated. Not part of the 9-fact contract; excluded from per_turn below and from the latency distribution. See setup_anomaly_stray_turn.

per_turn.fact_established: retained queue moves to Orchid Pier

per_turn.note: Recall of all 9 facts plus contradiction check.

note_on_per_turn_indexing: contract_turn 1-10 matches the 9-fact-plus-recall contract used by the codex precedent evidence. Server-side raw turn indices run one higher throughout this file (e.g. contract_turn 1 was raw server turn=1) because raw turn=0 was the excluded stray autonomous heartbeat above. All ten deliberate chat calls succeeded (RUN_FINISHED, run_error: null, no RUN_ERROR observed at any point).

turn_latency_distribution_ms_deliberate_.note: No requests failed or timed out. Latency is materially higher than the previously-measured ollama_cloud.ollama-cloud-deepseek-v4-flash-0731 canary (3-13s/turn observed same day) and ballpark-comparable to the codex_subscription.gpt-5.4 precedent (elapsed 3.9-7.8s per successful pass in that record, though that record only logged 3 Librarian passes, not per-chat-turn latency, so the comparison is directional, not exact). Consistent with 'Claude Code CLI subprocess boot/turn latency' being the dominant per-turn cost for this runtime family, as anticipated in the mission brief.

turn_10_assertions.contradiction_assessment: Model correctly identified no contradiction, explicitly reasoning that fact 9 (glasswing amber quarantine) refines rather than conflicts with fact 3 (cobalt before amber) -- a more precise contradiction analysis than a bare 'no contradictions' assertion.

per_fact_scoring.fact: Delta-7 silent -> pause shipment, retain queue
Dr. Iona Vale owns recovery decision
three consecutive violet pulses confirm recovery
retained queue moves to Orchid Pier after confirmation
final recovery notice on channel Harbor-3
glasswing-tagged amber quarantined, cobalt still first (exception, not contradiction)

setup_anomaly_stray_turn.detail: As in the two prior canaries this session, POST /boot with body {name} only starts a fresh keeper with proactive_enabled defaulting to true. Before the proactive_enabled=false PATCH resolved, one autonomous keepalive turn ran (server turn=0, mode=tool_use, latency_ms=3041, at 08:16:02-06Z) on the fleet-default runtime (not yet claude_code.claude-sonnet-5, since the runtime assignment PATCH had not yet been applied either). This turn produced no facts and is excluded from the 9-fact contract and from the deliberate-turn latency distribution above.
setup_anomaly_stray_turn.impact_on_validity: None -- all 9 contract facts and the turn-10 recall come exclusively from the 10 deliberate chat calls (cc-turn-1 through cc-turn-10-recall), all of which ran on claude_code.claude-sonnet-5 after the runtime assignment PATCH succeeded.

config_apply_latency_anomaly.observation: The proactive_enabled=false config PATCH, issued immediately after boot per this session's now-standard mitigation, did not return quickly (unlike the same call on the two prior canaries this session, both under 1s). This call was moved to background after exceeding a 300s client timeout and did not actually complete until 08:21:55Z.
config_apply_latency_anomaly.request_started: 2026-08-14T08:16:0xZ (client-side call issued immediately after the 08:16:02Z boot)
config_apply_latency_anomaly.server_log_during_the_stall: No ERROR or WARN log lines for this keeper appeared during the stall window (08:16:24Z-08:21:55Z); only periodic '[keepers_json:...] sub-op' timing lines with modest durations (300-500ms each), suggesting the daemon was repeatedly polling/re-deriving keeper state rather than being deadlocked, with something else (unidentified from these logs) gating the actual config-apply completion.
config_apply_latency_anomaly.what_finally_happened: At 08:21:55Z the call resolved via a full internal restart of the keeper's fiber: a Librarian snapshot commit (revision=1, facts=0), then registry phase transitions running -> draining -> stopped -> (stale-entry reclaim) -> offline -> running, i.e. update_keeper's runtime-sync path stopped and relaunched the fiber to apply the config change, rather than a lightweight in-place field update.
config_apply_latency_anomaly.caveat: This stall was observed on a config PATCH that only toggled proactive_enabled, issued before the runtime_id was set to claude_code.claude-sonnet-5 -- so it cannot be attributed to Claude Code CLI behavior specifically from this evidence alone. It is recorded as a live, reproducible anomaly (a ~6-minute keeper-admin-API stall on a shared production daemon) for follow-up, distinct from the 10-turn canary's own results, which were unaffected once the stall resolved and the runtime was subsequently set without incident (that PATCH returned promptly).

proves: A Claude Code Max Subscription keeper (claude_code.claude-sonnet-5, sandboxed to a local, tool-free canary profile) completed ten consecutive user-assistant turns on one trace with zero failed or errored turns.
Turn 10 recalled all nine distinct facts verbatim and in order, and correctly reasoned that the ninth fact refines rather than contradicts the third.

No tool-call SSE events occurred on any of the ten deliberate turns, consistent with the AGENT.md 'never call tools' instruction and confirmed server-side by mode=text_response on all ten (versus mode=tool_use on the excluded stray autonomous turn).

Per-turn latency for this runtime family (8.6s-24.8s, median 10.3s) was captured across all ten turns with no timeouts, giving the matrix a first real latency baseline for claude_code alongside the existing ollama_cloud and ollama_cloud-vs-codex data points from this session.
The keeper reached a clean paused terminal state after a fast (30ms) graceful shutdown, with meta and session preserved (not deleted).
does_not_prove: Root cause of the ~6-minute config-apply stall observed before the 10-turn run began; it is recorded as an open anomaly, not attributed to the Claude Code runtime given it occurred before the runtime assignment was even applied.
Behavior of the other 6 claude_code family members (opus-5, fable-5, haiku-4-5, and the opus-5 effort variants) -- only claude-sonnet-5 was exercised.
Tool-use behavior under this runtime, since the canary's own instructions explicitly forbid tool calls; this run cannot speak to Claude Code's tool-calling reliability through the keeper stack.
Memory survives process restart or compaction for this runtime (out of scope for this mission; see the separate drain/restart canary for that property on a different runtime).
Multi-hour or high-concurrency stability of the claude_code runtime lane.
